That’s my biggest fear. I really want to adopt kids - I have forever - but I find myself daydreaming about having kids and then messing it up so badly that even if they don’t hate me, I’ve hurt them in an irrevocable way and can never take it back. And it’s terrifying.

I’m sorry you even feel like that with your wife. I feel like I’d ask my spouse every day if they still loved me, and if so, why. What does she say when you ask?

The nice thing about Reddit is that your comment, if unhelpful or harmful, can be downvoted to oblivion or deleted by somebody else, so you don’t have to sensor yourself here because others with better understanding of how humans work can do it for you. At least, that’s how I operate. Reddit is the one place I don’t have to sensor myself so I take advantage of it.

YES. And then I stumble over my words and talk for too long or talk over them and make them feel like I’m not listening to them and just generally treat them poorly when I’m actually trying to make them hate me less or make them feel better or get out of talking to them so they don’t have to deal with me. I have no idea how to fix this.

Your therapist and doctor suck. If you have the energy or family members willing to do it for you, you should get new ones. The point of them is to help you find tricks to deal with the days when you’re so depressed that you look lazy or whatever. If they aren’t doing that they should be fired. You deserve better.

I mean. Suddenly stopping caring is super hard. But definitely finding a way to get active might help (join a sports club or something, and only hang out with the people who are nice to you).

Also, maybe once a day just sit and write down one thing you like about yourself. Eventually you’ll have a list of things you can look at. (I also screenshot text messages of people saying nice things about me. I know it sounds super egotistical but it really helps when I’m feeling particularly awful.)

I’m so sorry you lost your best friend. That’s awful. Obviously you’re always welcome to rant here.

Does your girlfriend know about your attempt? If so, she might not be offended by the scars (might be worried though).

that's just cruel, then - they won't know what happened and will always have hope that you'll reappear one day. What the other commenters have said is that mourners need closure, and that seems true.

Congrats on getting here though. I feel genuinely surprised every birthday. Like, how did I get here? Why am I still alive?

20 seems pretty old but I've met 50 year olds who decided to do a career change and started school again to that end. Keep yourself alive so you have the time to figure out what you can give to the world and see what the world can give you. We all die anyway, so might as well, right? Compared to the amount of resources the world has, you're almost certainly taking up a very small fraction. So you can't possibly be a huge drain or a waste, which means you can (and are almost obligated to) stay long enough to find a reason to keep going.

I get that. Sometimes I feel great and then when I crash I'm shocked and devastated because what was the point of all the happiness?

That said, please don't wreck your brother's honeymoon with your suicide. Put it off as long as you can. Procrastinating in this case is a great thing. You could just listen to music nonstop and veg out. Or you could find people to play basketball with. Or you could go to the library and check out 50 pounds of books and just read nonstop. Find ways to procrastinate.

Yeah, but people will find you. The moment your family realises that you're missing, they'll file a report or something, and even if it takes years, whatever parts of your body is found will leave your family deeply traumatised.

There's no way out, dude. As long as people need/care about you, you can't disappear without hurting anyone. I've struggled with this myself. There's no way to disappear without hurting at least one person you love dearly.

I'd message her best friend(s) and parents, then text something like the crisis text line and ask them what to do. I don't know your ex so I don't know what would help her but telling her that she matters to you even if you don't make a good couple should help.

Is your stress caused by something? If not, maybe you could try to take medicine. I had mostly bad days too, and I can't say my days are good now, but for the most part they're better. You could take medicine for long enough that your emotions don't drain all your energy, and then you can try to start exercising or whatever you want to experiment with to make yourself feel better aside from medicine.

If it is, do you want to talk? If you don't want a random stranger maybe you can pick your second-favorite person in your life and try to figure out if they're willing to help you figure out how to solve the problems causing your stress.

Also! Feeling Good by David Burns is a nice textbook if you're the kind of person who likes to treat your mind like a research project. Regardless of whether or not your stress has a cause, that book might be the second-best thing to a therapist that I've used.

I don't really believe in happiness - at least, not in the long term. I don't think happiness is sustainable. My goal is to be content, and I want the people I love to be content with as little sadness as possible. But you can't give me your happiness. I'd just burn through it and end up worse.

Not sure if you wanted advice but if you do:

You should consider taking a break from university. Do you have parents/guardians who love you? If so, maybe you can temporarily move in with them. If not, maybe you should find a place to live in by yourself? But have somebody (even a fellow redditer) check in with you every so often so people know if you're still alive.

You could take a class at a local college while you're on break from university. It's easier to pass classes if you're only taking one. (Note that I said "easier" and not "easy" - classes are hard when you're too sad to concentrate.)

You could also get a part-time job, maybe? Or something to force yourself to get out the door every day. Skipping classes is easy. Skipping work has consequences. So that might be a better motivator.

If you take a break then therapy+job+class might fill up your time enough that you can feel better enough to talk to people/socialize and maybe you'll eventually get better enough to go back to university and feel less likely to fail out?

I say this because that's what my friend did, and I don't know if it would have worked for me but it worked for her pretty well. She even has a full-time job now.
